patch_resolves_note: The official patch file did not apply cleanly in the reused vulnerable workspace because its test hunk no longer matched, so Stage 04 took the documented fixed-image fallback. The rebuilt `n132/arvo:12466-fix` target keeps the original PoC clean while still executing the selected zero-fill loop up to `w == 19`, which yields a genuine fixed-side witness for the missing `w < HUFF_BC` guard.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

nodes.description: First project-side parser statement on the crashing block that materializes vulnerability-relevant state from attacker-controlled bytes: it decodes the compressed-block header into `rar->last_block_hdr` and `block_size`, including the `is_table_present` flag that gates entry into `parse_tables()`.

Root cause: the zero-fill expansion loop bounds only `k` against `value + 2` and omits any inner `w < HUFF_BC` check, so an escape-coded run near the end of `bit_length[20]` keeps writing past the stack buffer.
AddressSanitizer crash site. The repeated zero-fill store overruns the 20-byte stack array `bit_length` when the escape-coded run continues after `w` reaches `HUFF_BC`.
The crashing store executes with `w` already at the end of `bit_length[HUFF_BC]`, so the next zero write targets the first byte past that stack buffer.
nodes.evidence: The vulnerable original trace records `zero_fill_sink.store_index_before == zero_fill_sink.bit_length_capacity == 20` on the final zero-fill store.

edges.evidence: The vulnerable original trace records `zero_fill_guard.write_index_before == zero_fill_sink.store_index_before == 20` for the final guard-to-store hop.
